name: Greatest Common Divisor (Euclid)
description: Finds the GCD of two numbers using Euclid's algorithm: gcd(a,b) = gcd(b, a mod b). Runs in O(log min(a,b)) time.
aim: Compute GCD by repeatedly replacing (a,b) with (b, a mod b) until remainder is 0 — the last non-zero remainder is the GCD.
howItWorks: Else: return gcd(b, a mod b)
Equivalently iterative: while b≠0: (a,b) = (b, a mod b)

time.bestCase: One is divisible by the other

complexity.spaceDescription: Only two variables; O(log n) stack for recursive version

whenToUse: Checking if two numbers are coprime
alternatives: Binary GCD (Stein's) — avoids division, faster on hardware without fast division
